published_prior_art.cite: LuedtkeVanDerLaan2016OptimalValue — optimal-value inference under a supplied observation law, not the history-dependent zero-exposure observational-equivalence diagnostic.
PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits — uses compatible smoothness-margin classes but does not supply this benchmark-exposure witness.
CaiLow2004 + KaufmannCappeGarivier2016Complexity — fixed-experiment expected-length modulus and adaptive bandit change of measure, respectively.
SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign — finite-arm expected gap-estimation error versus regret, rather than all-procedure honest width for the contextual nonlinear targeting gain.

HuKallusMao2022SmoothContextualBandits + BibautEtAl2021PostContextualBanditInference — selective exploration and regular fixed-policy inference, not semi-infinite local-alternative allocation saturation under a welfare budget.

SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign; PonomarevSemenova2024LowerConfidenceBand; PraharajKhamaru2025AvoidingPriceAdaptivity — none minimizes uniformly honest two-sided expected width over welfare-feasible contextual designs for the positive-part gain.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a finite-arm stochastic MAB, defines expected absolute treatment-gap estimation error, proves a regret-error product lower bound, and gives a finite-sample estimator-error guarantee for its EXP3E design.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1 and 7, stochastic-bandit setup and Lemma 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source assumes independent draws from arm distributions under adaptive arm choice and gives its change-of-measure inequality for bandit models.

source_verification_receipts.version: author preprint arXiv:1110.6084; corroboration only because the cited AOS primary version was not tool-accessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The preprint states bounded-reward contextual-bandit smoothness and margin conditions, the αβ≤d nontrivial regime, and the ABSE regret upper exponent; it attributes matching K=2 lower bounds to earlier sources.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint, latest revision reported September 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops one-sided lower confidence bands for optimal welfare, relates first-order behavior to margin separation, and gives robust moment-inequality-based alternatives under nonuniqueness.

The paper establishes stability, Wald inference for fixed linear functionals, and near-minimax regret for a penalized EXP4 linear contextual-bandit design; it does not state a uniform honest-width frontier for a nonregular positive-part target.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Split the feasibility citation into a quoted bounded-reward Perchet–Rigollet result, an explicit cited K=2 minimax-lower source, and a short Gaussian-tail transfer lemma; record exact AOS locators before using it as the early-kill boundary.

For the allocation handle, work a finite dyadic two-cell instance from primitive means through S_Q(w), B(w), D(w), and its welfare-priced quotas; this will make any later saturation or capacity obstruction falsifiable rather than purely asymptotic.
State the completed-frontier comparison against a named offline positive-part-functional rate at ρ≈T, including the exact estimator/class used for that sanity reduction.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the complete-width-frontier kernel, while obtaining the primary Perchet–Rigollet locator and a separately cited minimax-lower source for the feasibility sanity reduction.
